issue_context.title: Remove PreserveDependency from SR class
issue_context.body: The `PreserveDependencyAttribute` should be no longer needed as the illinker can now recognize RunClassConstructor method call.
comments: I couldn't figure out the best area label to add to this issue. Please help me learn by adding exactly one [area label](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/docs/area-owners.md).

review_comments:
1. If the .cctor has any side effects, linker would not know to keep it and the end result would be to lose those side-effects -> bad. So I added the attribute to make sure we keep it.
2. As per https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/36330 linker now handles `RunClassConstructor` as an intrinsic and will preserve the `.cctor` as necessary. So no annotation is necessary. And also none of the annotations we currently have would work anyway.

I'm questioning the validity of removing the .cctor if _anything_ on the type is used.  It's not uncommon to use a .cctor for side-effects, e.g. initializing something in the system.  We did/do it ourselves in a variety of cases, e.g.
https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/blob/c74ea81f2ddad07dc05d695d8244fb2ece7e398d/src/Common/src/Interop/Unix/System.Net.Http.Native/Interop.Initialization.cs#L10-L20
Is it only removed in the case of beforefieldinit?  Even if so, I've still seen numerous cases where that would break things.

1. I don't know the answer - I'll have to look into that (I don't remember the rules which linker uses to remove .cctors)
2. We don't have a way to annotate that using the data flow - linker will issue a warning. If I know what the type could be, then I can add the `DynamicDependencyAttribute` and suppress the warning. If I don't, it's simply a pattern we don't have a solution for (just like 10s of other reflection patterns) - maybe "yet"?

I wrote the answer to 1 here: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/36277#discussion_r424261042. It wasn't really needed (we call RunClassConstructor not because of some side effects, but just to frontload it in case there's a problem with running it). If the linker decided to remove the cctor, it would be fine for this to be a no-op. There are legit situations when linker can remove the cctor when it knows it won't be triggered (a beforefieldinit cctor when none of the static fields are accessed is provably not needed because it won't trigger, except for these reflection-like APIs that we analyze/warn about).

2. The cctor would be kept if constructors are kept, so we do have an annotation for this. Cctors are returned from the `Type.GetConstructors` APIs. What we don't have is a way to annotate `RuntimeTypeHandle`. We could add it, but this feels like a niche. The uses in WPF are hopeless for dataflow analysis to analyze anyway (they run on stuff read from XAML).

The part of (1) that I'm still confused about is why calling `RuntimeHelpers.RunClassConstructor` would force the preservation of the `.cctor`? (And as an off-shoot of that - why should it cause a linker warning?) If the `.cctor` can be trimmed, or if it must be preserved, is a decision that should be made irregardless of someone calling `RuntimeHelpers.RunClassConstructor` on the Type.
OK, that example clears it up for me. Thanks for the explanation.
